scope: Two generated development coding tasks using normal Codex shell/edit tools. Both arms actually edit app.py and execute tests. Not a benchmark score or a whole-project estimate.
hypothesis: Reviewed Headroom reversible search/run folds reduce whole-task native model tokens without losing observed repair quality when applied to real shell output before inference.

conditions.compact: live headroom-lossless route, same prompts and environment

quality_gate: All four cells must preserve fixtures/tests, pass visible tests and independent post-run checks. No retrospective fixture edits or repeats.
acceptance: All quality checks pass and pooled whole-task native total tokens are at least 5% lower. Candidate route must demonstrably transform actual model-facing shell results in both compact cells. Report per-case results and any regression. Timing descriptive only.
accounting: Count every native response once by ID, all input/output and extra tool calls/retrievals. Cached input is already included. Record original and forwarded request bodies/hashes and source hashes, transform CPU time, wall time and all failed attempts. Analyst/development costs are additional research overhead, not first-use savings.
security: No Headroom package installation. Apache-2.0 stdlib-only lossless_compaction.py pinned at 2d3ee51846435ef5b320eea4806af14e602b0d8c, with a reviewed local logging adapter. No native extension, package initialization, network telemetry or model downloads.
execution: Sequential alternating order, fresh workspace/session per cell, same model, no automatic request or stream retries. Stop on uncertain invocation. Preserve every attempt and grade. Ordinary Codex tools only; no special read_evidence views or replay MCP.
rollback: Keep global default at verified progress-only unless both compact coding cells transform and the complete quality/token gate passes. The full-lossless route remains experimental on any failure. Baseline route always available.
